----
# Mid-Sprint Check-in: @arjunsb26

## Question 1: What did you implement so far in the sprint, and what remains?

My main work so far is #14, the milestone burndown chart, which was carried over from Sprint 1. PR #77 merged on 10-09. The milestone page now draws a burndown with an ideal line and a projected finish date. It marks where scope was added or removed, and hovering over a day lists the items that changed on it. A checkbox, saved in the URL, adds pull requests to the chart. The history is rebuilt from timeline comments, so it needed no migration. The PR has Go unit, integration, Vitest and e2e tests. After review I fixed stale responses when the toggle is clicked quickly, and a projection that was measured from the wrong day.

What remains is all of my Sprint 2 load. I have no issues on the Sprint 2 milestone yet. I need to pick two medium issues, write their specs with a design decision, get them peer-reviewed, and then implement them with Tech Debt sections. I also need to draw the UML diagrams for one of them, file my AI logs, and review a teammate's PR.

## Question 2: What is one thing you learned about the codebase or about software engineering practice?

I learned that a permission check on a route doesn't always mean the data behind it is safe to show. The milestone pages let in anyone who can read issues *or* pull requests, so adding my chart endpoint to the same route group was not enough. A viewer who could read issues but not pull requests would still have seen pull request titles in the chart. The server now counts and lists a kind only if the viewer can read it, and two integration tests turn off each unit and check that nothing leaks. I confirmed that both tests fail when the check is removed, because a test that never fails proves nothing.

I also learned that Gitea's timeline comments work as an event log. Replaying them lets you rebuild the past without storing daily snapshots, but the replay has to end on the database's current state. Otherwise the chart can disagree with the progress bar right above it.

## Question 3: What is one thing you would do differently?

I would check my work against the acceptance criteria before calling it done, not after. When I asked the AI whether #14 was complete, it found that the first version had missed three criteria: the scope markers, the hover details and the pull request toggle. Adding them late meant a second round of commits, more tests and another merge from main. If I had kept the criteria list open as a checklist while I worked, I would have caught those gaps on the first day.

I would also start my Sprint 2 issues sooner. Finishing #14 took the first part of the sprint, and I put off choosing new issues until it merged. That leaves the spec reviews, which depend on teammates' turnaround, crowded into the second week. Writing the specs while #14 was in review would have kept both moving at once.----

## Goals for the mid-check

1. **Claim your load today.** The team's code-suggestions feature (#151) has three medium issues with no assignee, and they fit with what your teammates are already building:
   - **#158 S5:** suggest a change across several lines. This builds on S1 (#154, vvchopra) and S2 (#155, controlled-opposition).

   - **#160 S7:** create and apply suggestions through the API.

   Taking two of them meets the 2-medium load. **S5 + S7** depend least on S3, which hasn't merged yet. Assign yourself and add them to the Sprint 3 milestone.
2. **Write the specs and get them peer-reviewed by about Nov 14.** Each needs a user story, acceptance criteria, an estimate and a design decision with at least two alternatives.
3. **Review a teammate's PR.** #161, #162 and #163 are all waiting for review. #163 (S1 rendering) and #162 (S2 button) are the ones your S5 builds on, so reviewing one of them also prepares you for your own work.
4. **Implement and open PRs by about Nov 17.** Each PR needs a `## Tech Debt` section. That leaves a two-day buffer for review rounds before the Nov 19 deadline.

CSCI 435/535 — Software Engineering[¶](#csci-435535-software-engineering "Permanent link")
==========================================================================================

Welcome to CSCI 435/535. This semester, six teams will each work on a real, established open-source project using modern agentic AI tooling as part of their software engineering workflow: agile sprints, code review, CI, testing, and real project management.

Announcements[¶](#announcements "Permanent link")
-------------------------------------------------

November 12, 2026 — **Schedule update:** reading assignments on Blackboard are due **Nov 18, 20, and 30**, plus optional extra credit due **Dec 4**. See the [Schedule](schedule/).

November 4, 2026 — **Sprint 3 is open.** All deliverables are due **November 19 at 11:59 PM**; the mid-sprint check-in (D7), with at least one code PR open or merged, is due **November 12 at 11:59 PM**. New this sprint: **mutation testing** (replaces the UML diagrams), a **Test Evidence** section in every PR, and a **suite health** section in the report. See the [Sprint 3 requirements](sprint3/) for full details.

Sprint 3: Project Development & Testing[¶](#sprint-3-project-development-testing "Permanent link")
==================================================================================================

**Nov 3 – Nov 19 · All deliverables due Nov 19, 11:59 PM (mid-sprint check-in due Nov 12) · 100 points (12% of course grade)**

Sprint 3 continues the development of your project and puts the focus on **testing**: how well your tests check what your code is supposed to do. The issue backlog, PR workflow, and general expectations carry forward; see [Sprint 1](../sprint1/) and [Sprint 2](../sprint2/) for anything not explicitly changed here. This page covers what is **new or different** in Sprint 3.

* * *

Sprint 3 at a glance

**Key dates:** Nov 12: check-in + at least one code PR (open or merged) · Nov 19: everything else

**Important rules (they cost the most points):**

*   No merge without an approval on the latest commit.
*   Spec review on the issue, saying what was checked.
*   Every code PR links its issue.
*   Real AI logs.
*   Test Evidence table in every PR; expected values not copied from the code's output.
*   Mutation testing with a tool, before and after reports committed.
*   Your team introduces no new test failures; skipped tests and disabled checks need an issue.

Unfamiliar with a term?

Check the [Glossary](../glossary/) for definitions of terms used throughout this page.

* * *

### Before you begin[¶](#before-you-begin "Permanent link")

*   **Check your AI log setup** against the [AI Log Instructions](../ai-logs/) before your first session.
*   **Read "Things that must improve"** below. These issues were observed in Sprint 2 and will be graded strictly.
*   **Record your baseline early** (see D8): the test results at your Sprint 2 release tag (`-csci435-s2`), from CI or by running the relevant test suites locally. It helps you find hardening issues and get the mutation tool running.
*   **Try the mutation testing tool early** (see D6), on any existing file in the part of the code you work on. Do not wait until your PRs are ready.

* * *

### What is new in Sprint 3[¶](#what-is-new-in-sprint-3 "Permanent link")

*   **Mutation testing** (D6): a new individual deliverable. It **replaces** the UML diagrams from Sprint 2.
*   **Test evidence section** in every PR description (D4).
*   **Hardening issues**: one of your issues may be a hardening issue (D1).
*   **Suite health section** in the sprint report (D8).
*   **Mid-sprint check-in requires an open PR** (D7), due Nov 12.

Team feature for Sprints 3–4

Each team will be assigned a larger feature that spans Sprints 3 and 4. The instructor or TA will post it as an issue in your team's issue tracker and notify your team when it is posted. You will likely need to split it into sub-issues.

* * *

### Things that must improve from Sprint 2[¶](#things-that-must-improve-from-sprint-2 "Permanent link")

These issues were observed in Sprint 2 and will be graded strictly in Sprint 3.

**1\. Open PRs early.** In Sprint 2, most PRs were opened in the last two days, which left no time for review. In Sprint 3, you need a code PR by the mid-sprint check-in (see D7).

**2\. Independent approval before merging.** A PR is merged only after a teammate approves its **latest commit**. Merging without an approval, or after pushing new commits since the approval, is not allowed. Once approved, the author may merge. To keep reviews moving, request the review on GitHub and notify your reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond (approve or request changes) within 24 hours.

**3\. Spec reviews must be visible and show what was checked.** Before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment on the issue itself. The comment states what the reviewer checked: whether each acceptance criterion is clear and testable, which cases were considered (and whether they are covered), and whether the scope fits. If the reviewer finds problems, they list them and the author updates the spec. If the spec is good, the reviewer says so and approves, but "Looks good!" with nothing about what was checked is not acceptable.

**4\. Link PRs and issues.** Every code PR must link the issue it addresses, so the PR can be checked against the spec. Use `Closes #<issue>` in the PR description so the issue closes automatically when the PR is merged, and attach issues and code PRs to the `Sprint 3` milestone.

**5\. AI logs must be real logs.** A log shows your prompts and the AI's output (SpecStory format recommended; see the [AI Log Instructions](../ai-logs/)). The following are **not** logs and receive no full credit: summaries of a session, paraphrased prompts, a share link to a chat, or tool output without the prompts that produced it. File names must follow `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log from the issue or PR it documents.

**6\. The sprint report must render.** Check that tables and links display correctly on GitHub (no escaped `\|` or `\[`). Use the Sprint 3 sections, not a copy of a previous report.

* * *

### Deliverables[¶](#deliverables "Permanent link")

#### D1 - Sprint Backlog[¶](#d1-sprint-backlog "Permanent link")

Same process as Sprint 2 ([D1](../sprint2/#d1-sprint-backlog)), including the priority on carryovers: unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into your Sprint 3 backlog first, or you document on the issue why they are dropped.

**Scope minimums for Sprint 3** (same as Sprint 2):

Role

Minimum issues

Each CSCI 435 member

at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent story points)

Each CSCI 535 (grad) member

at least 2 medium issues + 1 additional small issue (or equivalent story points)

**Scope must be justified.** Each issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why: which components it touches and how much change you expect. The instructor or TA may reclassify an issue whose scope is clearly overstated.

**Hardening issues (optional).** One of your issues may be a _hardening issue_: work that makes the existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources:

*   **Your baseline run** (see D8): failing tests, flaky tests, or broken CI checks on `main`.
*   **Tech debt your team recorded** in the "Introduced" and "Encountered" fields of your Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs.
*   **Known bugs** found in reviews, after merging, or by teammates.
*   **The upstream issue tracker**, for bugs in the parts of the system your team works on.

A hardening issue is scoped like any other issue (see the scope justification above). It must also include evidence that the problem is fixed:

*   **Bug fix:** a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
*   **Flaky test:** the root cause, and enough repeated runs of that test before and after the fix to show the change (for example, 20 runs for a unit test or 10 for an E2E test).
*   **Broken or missing CI check:** links to CI runs before and after the fix.
*   **Failing tests in the baseline:** pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group of failures.

Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause counts as small at most.

**Team feature.** When the team feature issue is posted (see the box under "What is new in Sprint 3"), split it into sub-issues, each with its own owner, spec (D2), and scope. Link each sub-issue to the feature issue. Sub-issues count toward your scope minimum like any other issue. When the feature is posted, add its sub-issues to your Sprint 3 milestone and adjust your backlog as needed.

Create a `Sprint 3` milestone in GitHub and attach all selected issues to it.

**What to provide in D8 (Sprint report):** link to the Sprint 3 milestone and the rationale for your backlog decisions.

* * *

#### D2 - Requirements Specification[¶](#d2-requirements-specification "Permanent link")

Same format and requirements as Sprint 1 ([D2](../sprint1/#d2-requirements-specification)). Specs must be written and reviewed before coding begins; see item 3 in "Things that must improve" for what counts as a review.

Hardening issues use a bug format (include the observed and expected behaviors, the steps to reproduct the issue, and other details about the issue) when they fix a defect. Otherwise, use a short task format: the problem, the goal, acceptance criteria, and other necessary details.

* * *

#### D3 - Design Decisions[¶](#d3-design-decisions "Permanent link")

Same as Sprint 2 ([D3](../sprint2/#d3-design-decisions)): each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and explains the choice.

* * *

#### D4 - Code Changes and Pull Requests[¶](#d4-code-changes-and-pull-requests "Permanent link")

Same workflow as Sprint 2 ([D4](../sprint2/#d4-code-changes-and-pull-requests)), including **the Tech Debt section**. Sprint 3 adds a **Test Evidence** section to every PR description. It replaces the "how it was tested" part of the description, so you don't write it twice.

`## Test Evidence  | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value | |---|---|---|---| | AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |  **Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]  **AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]`

How to fill it in:

*   **One row per acceptance criterion** from D2. For bug reports, use the Expected Behavior instead. For PRs that change no product behavior (for example, CI changes), write "N/A" and explain why.
*   **Test(s):** the test name (and file, if not obvious). If you checked the AC manually, write `Manual:` followed by the steps and what you saw. If an AC is tested both automatically and manually, list both in the same row.
*   **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E`, or `manual`.
*   **Source of expected value:** where the expected result in your test comes from. Use one of: `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or `other` (explain). **The current output of your own code is not a valid source**; a test whose expected value was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
*   **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
*   You may use AI to draft this section, but you are responsible for checking that it is accurate.

Example:

Acceptance criterion

Test(s)

Level

Source of expected value

AC1: An end date before the start date is rejected with an error

`outOfOffice.schema.test.ts` > rejects end before start

unit

AC

AC2: The away badge appears on the booking page during the out-of-office window

`booking-ooo.e2e.ts` > shows away badge in window

E2E

AC

AC3: The badge text is readable in dark mode

Manual: enabled dark mode, opened the booking page during the window → badge text is readable

manual

issue discussion

**Not tested automatically, and why:** AC3 depends on visual contrast, which our test setup does not check.

#### D6 - Mutation Testing _(new)_[¶](#d6-mutation-testing-new "Permanent link")

This is a new individual deliverable.

**What it is.** A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (_mutants_), such as flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is _killed_. If all tests pass, the mutant _survived_: your tests did not notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

**What to do.** For **one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests** (CSCI 535: **two** such issues; your small issue may be one of them):

1.  Run a mutation testing tool on the **source files changed by your PR(s)** for that issue. Do not run it on the whole project.
2.  Using the tool's report, analyze every surviving mutant: is it _equivalent_ (it behaves exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a gap in your tests? If there are more than 10 surviving mutants, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines your PR added or changed.
3.  Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a surviving mutant** that revealed a gap. Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no surviving mutant reveals a gap (all are killed or equivalent), say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4.  **Answer the questions in the template below**.

**Evidence.** Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`; Gremlins: `--output=<file>.json`; go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file). Commit the report from your first run and from your re-run as `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt` for go-mutesting). The mutation scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.

**A tool is required.** Manual mutation does not count.

Stack

Tool

TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest (Actual Budget, Cal.diy, Excalidraw, Outline, Gitea frontend)

[StrykerJS](https://stryker-mutator.io/) with the [Vitest runner](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/vitest-runner/)

TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)

[StrykerJS](https://stryker-mutator.io/) with the [Jest runner](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/jest-runner/)

Go (Gitea backend)

[Gremlins](https://gremlins.dev/) or [go-mutesting](https://github.com/avito-tech/go-mutesting)

**Set it up early.** Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services, and choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits the configuration they used. You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to), as long as you run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

**Common problems** to watch for:

*   **The tool stops before mutating.** Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any of the selected tests fail, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where your baseline run helps).
*   **Tests run against built code.** If your tests run against compiled output (for example, a `dist` folder) instead of the source, mutants in the source are never seen by the tests. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing, or choose tests that run on source.
*   **Tests need services.** Some test suites need a database or another service running. Start them before running the tool.
*   **False survivors.** If you limit which tests run (for example, with Vitest's `dir` option), make sure the tests that cover the mutated files are included. Otherwise, mutants that some test would catch are reported as survived or not covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
*   **Long runs.** Mutating only the files changed by your PR keeps run time manageable.

If you are blocked

If you cannot get the tool to run, first ask your teammates: someone may already have a working setup. If you are still stuck, tell the TA **as early as possible**, with the errors you got and the AI log of what you tried. The TA will help you debug it. If it still cannot be made to work, the TA may approve running the tool on a different issue or a different part of your code instead. Problems reported at the end of the sprint will not excuse a missing D6.

**Submission:** `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md`, using this template:

``# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <issue title>  **PR(s):** #...  **Tool:** ...  **Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]  **Command:** `...` **Reports:** [before](reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json) · [after](reports/<issue#>-<username>-after.json) **Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%  ## Surviving mutants  | Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why | |---|---|---|---| | | | | |  ## New or strengthened test  Commit: [link] · Test: [file > test name] · Kills: [mutant location]  ## Questions  1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests? 2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain. 3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct? If AI was not used, write "N/A."``

=================== #158
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on S1, S3

As a reviewer, I want to select a range of lines and suggest a replacement for all of them so that
I can propose changes bigger than one line.

### User Scenario

Ana shift-clicks lines 18 to 22 in the Files tab, clicks `+`, then "Suggest change". The block is
pre-filled with those five lines. She rewrites them as three lines. Ben sees a five-red /
three-green diff and applies it.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a reviewer shift-selects a contiguous range of new-side lines in one hunk, when
  they open the comment form, then the comment is anchored to the whole range and the header says
  "Lines 18–22".
- [ ] AC2: Given a multi-line suggestion, when rendered, then all lines in the range show as
  removed and the block's lines as added (S1 behaviour for a range).
- [ ] AC3: Given a multi-line suggestion, when applied, then exactly that range is replaced, and it
  is refused as outdated if any line in the range changed (S3 AC3 for a range).
- [ ] AC4: Given a selection that spans two hunks or both sides of the diff, when the reviewer tries
  to comment, then the selection is refused with a message.
- [ ] AC5: Given existing single-line comments after the upgrade, when shown and applied, then they
  behave exactly as before (range start = line).

### Out of Scope

- Ranges across files.


### Open Questions

- Maximum range length? (Proposed: the hunk's size; no separate cap.)

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Add a `start_line` column to `comment` (0 = single-line, as today) and keep `Line` as
the range end, so every existing comment is a valid single-line range.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Store the range inside the comment body or a JSON column.* No schema change, but the range
  can't be queried or invalidated with the existing code.
- *Create one linked comment per line.* Breaks the "one comment, one suggestion" model from S4.

**Rationale:** `Line` keeps its meaning, so `InvalidateCodeComments`, the API and old rows are
untouched; only code that cares about ranges reads `start_line`.

**Consequences:** Migration; `InvalidateCodeComments` should consider the whole range; S7's API
gains a start-line field.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

DB work
=================== #160
### User Story

As a bot or tool author, I want to create suggestions and apply them through `/api/v1` so that
automated reviewers (linters, formatters) can propose fixes that the author applies in Gitea.

### User Scenario

A lint bot posts a review via `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews` with a comment
whose body has a suggestion block. Ben applies it in the UI. A release script calls
`POST .../pulls/comments/{id}/suggestion/apply` to apply another one.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a review created through the existing API with a suggestion block in a code
  comment, when viewed in the UI, then it renders as a suggestion and can be applied (no API
  change needed; integration test proves it).
- [ ] AC2: Given a token with `write:repository` and push access to the head branch, when it POSTs
  the apply endpoint, then the commit is created and the response contains the commit SHA.
- [ ] AC3: Given missing permission, an outdated suggestion, an already applied one, or a stale
  `head_sha`, when the endpoint is called, then it returns 403 / 409 / 409 / 409 with a message and
  commits nothing.
- [ ] AC4: Given `GET` on a review comment, when the suggestion was applied, then the response
  includes `suggestion_applied_by` and `suggestion_applied_commit`.
- [ ] AC5: Swagger is regenerated and the swagger check passes.

### Out of Scope

- A batch apply endpoint, unless S6 has landed (then add `comment_ids[]`).


### Open Questions

- Should the API also accept a structured `suggestion` field instead of only markdown in `body`?


### Design Decision

**Decision:** No new create endpoint: suggestions stay markdown in the comment body. Add one apply
endpoint that takes `head_sha` and an optional `message` and calls S3's service.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A structured create endpoint (`path`, `lines`, `replacement`).* Easier for bots, but two ways to
  author the same thing that must render identically.
- *Mirror GitHub's API shape exactly.* GitHub has no apply endpoint to mirror.

**Rationale:** Bots already post review comments through the existing API, so they get
suggestions for free, and the service layer is shared with the UI.

**Consequences:** New route and swagger entry (`docs/routers-api-v1.md`), new fields on the comment
API struct (`docs/modules-structs.md`).

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Touches multiple components. Builds off S3
=================== #159
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on S3, S4

As a PR author, I want to pick several suggestions and apply them together so that my branch gets
one commit instead of one per suggestion.

### User Scenario

Ana leaves four suggestions on two files. Ben clicks **Add to batch** on three of them; a bar at the
bottom shows "3 suggestions selected · Apply". He applies them and the PR gets one commit changing
both files, and all three comments are marked applied.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given several selected suggestions, when applied, then one commit containing all of
  them is added and each is marked applied (S4) with that commit.
- [ ] AC2: Given two selected suggestions whose lines overlap, when the user tries to add the second
  to the batch, then it is refused with "overlaps another suggestion in this batch".
- [ ] AC3: Given one suggestion in the batch is outdated, when applied, then nothing is committed
  and the outdated one is named (all or nothing).
- [ ] AC4: Given the batch is left unapplied and the page is reloaded, then the batch is empty (it
  is not stored server-side).
- [ ] AC5: Permission, closed/merged PR and stale head rules are the same as S3.

### Out of Scope

- Batches across PRs; saving a batch for later.


### Open Questions

- Is there a maximum batch size? (Proposed: 50.)

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's service to take a list of comment IDs and build one
`ChangeRepoFiles` call with one entry per file, applying edits in a file bottom-up so earlier
replacements don't shift later line numbers.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Apply each suggestion as its own commit in a loop.* Easy, but not atomic: a failure halfway
  leaves a partial result, and it is not what the user asked for.
- *Store pending batches server-side.* Survives reloads, but needs a table and cleanup for
  something the user does in one sitting.

**Rationale:** One `ChangeRepoFiles` call is a single atomic commit, and bottom-up edits are a
simple, testable way to avoid line drift.

**Consequences:** S3's function signature changes; S7's batch endpoint reuses it.


### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

Touches a few different components

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package issues
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+
+	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
+)
+
+// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
+// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
+// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
+func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
+	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
+		return optional.None[string]()
+	}
+	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
+	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
+	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
+		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
+	}
+	return optional.Some(last[1:])
+}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/git"
	repo_service "gitea.dev/services/repository"
	files_service "gitea.dev/services/repository/files"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute(t *testing.T) {
	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
		user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		repo, err := repo_service.CreateRepositoryDirectly(t.Context(), user2, user2, repo_service.CreateRepoOptions{
			Name:             "test_suggestion",
			Readme:           "Default",
			AutoInit:         true,
			ObjectFormatName: git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(),
			DefaultBranch:    "master",
		}, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
			NewBranch: "suggestion-branch",
			Files: []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{
				Operation:     "update",
				TreePath:      "README.md",
				ContentReader: strings.NewReader("# Title\n\treturn err\n"),
			}},
		})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		testPullCreate(t, session, "user2", "test_suggestion", false, "master", "suggestion-branch", "Suggestion PR")
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{BaseRepoID: repo.ID, HeadBranch: "suggestion-branch"})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		commentURL := fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_suggestion/pulls/%d/files/reviews/comments", pr.Issue.Index)

		postComment := func(t *testing.T, origin, side, line string, extra map[string]string) *HTMLDoc {
			values := map[string]string{
				"origin":        origin,
				"content":       "```suggestion\n\treturn nil\n```",
				"side":          side,
				"line":          line,
				"path":          "README.md",
				"single_review": "true",
			}
			maps.Copy(values, extra)
			req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", commentURL, values)
			return NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK).Body)
		}

		for _, origin := range []string{"diff", "timeline"} { // repo/diff/comments.tmpl and view_content/conversation.tmpl
			t.Run(origin, func(t *testing.T) {
				markup := postComment(t, origin, "proposed", "2", nil).Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]").First()
				require.Equal(t, 1, markup.Length())
				assert.Equal(t, "\treturn err", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, "Suggested change", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-label", ""))
			})
		}

		t.Run("reply in the thread gets the attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
			first := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: 2, TreePath: "README.md"}, unittest.OrderBy("id ASC"))
			doc := postComment(t, "diff", "proposed", "2", map[string]string{"reply": strconv.FormatInt(first.ReviewID, 10)})
			markups := doc.Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]")
			assert.Equal(t, doc.Find(".render-content.markup").Length(), markups.Length()) // every comment in the thread, reply included
			assert.Equal(t, "\treturn err", markups.Last().AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
		})

		t.Run("old side gets no attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
			doc := postComment(t, "diff", "previous", "1", nil)
			assert.Equal(t, 0, doc.Find("[data-suggestion-original]").Length())
		})
	})
}

| `docs/testing.md` | authoritative test documentation; this doc summarises it |

## Conventions & invariants

- A Go package whose tests touch the database needs a `main_test.go` containing
  `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Without it the test DB is never
  initialised.
- Every DB-backed test calls `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` first, which reloads the fixtures, so
  tests do not depend on each other's writes.
- Adding a row to `models/fixtures/*.yml` means keeping denormalised counter columns
  (`num_issues`, `num_closed_issues`, ...) consistent, or `CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- Handler tests use `contexttest.MockContext` rather than constructing a `context.Context`
  by hand — see `services/context` for what the real one carries.
- Integration tests need Git LFS installed. The database comes from `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; empty
  defaults to SQLite, which is what you want locally.
- Frontend tests are Vitest, not Jest. Playwright is only for the e2e tier.

## Recipes

**Run one test.**

```sh
go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/   # or: make test-backend#TestName
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
```

**Add a DB-backed unit test.** Put `*_test.go` beside the code; add `main_test.go` with
`unittest.MainTest(m)` if the package has none; call `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`; load rows
with `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`; add fixture rows only if no existing row fits.

**Add an integration test.** New `tests/integration/<feature>_test.go`; `defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()`
at the top of the test; drive it through HTTP the way the neighbouring tests do. Do not add a
`TestMain` — `integration_test.go` already owns it.

import {queryElems} from '../utils/dom.ts';

function makeLine(kind: 'removed' | 'added', text: string): HTMLElement {
  const row = document.createElement('div');
  row.className = `markup-suggestion-line ${kind}`;
  const marker = document.createElement('span');
  marker.className = 'markup-suggestion-marker';
  marker.textContent = kind === 'removed' ? '-' : '+';
  const code = document.createElement('code');
  code.textContent = text; // never innerHTML: suggestion text is user input
  row.append(marker, code);
  return row;
}

// Replaces ```suggestion blocks in a PR code comment with a diff against the commented line.
// The server only sets data-suggestion-original on new-side code comments, so plain comments keep a code block.
export function initMarkupCodeSuggestion(elMarkup: HTMLElement): void {
  const original = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-original');
  if (original === null) return;
  const label = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-label')!;
  queryElems(elMarkup, 'code.language-suggestion', (elCode) => {
    const block = elCode.closest('.code-block-container') ?? elCode.closest('pre')!;
    // an empty fence renders "" (delete the line); otherwise every line ends with "\n", so one blank line is "\n"
    const raw = elCode.textContent;
    const diff = document.createElement('div');
    diff.className = 'markup-suggestion';
    const header = document.createElement('div');
    header.className = 'markup-suggestion-header';
    header.textContent = label;
    diff.append(header, makeLine('removed', original));
    if (raw !== '') {
      for (const line of raw.replace(/\r?\n$/, '').split(/\r?\n/)) diff.append(makeLine('added', line));
    }
    block.replaceWith(diff);
  });
}

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

// A bot posting a review through the existing API gets suggestions with no API change (#160 AC1).
func TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders(t *testing.T) {
	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
		const (
			commentedLine = "\treturn err" // line 2 of the head README, written below
			replacement   = "\treturn nil"
			suggestion    = "```suggestion\n" + replacement + "\n```"
		)

		user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		repo, err := repo_service.CreateRepositoryDirectly(t.Context(), user2, user2, repo_service.CreateRepoOptions{
			Name:             "test_api_suggestion",
			Readme:           "Default",
			AutoInit:         true,
			ObjectFormatName: git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(),
			DefaultBranch:    "master",
		}, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
			NewBranch: "suggestion-branch",
			Files: []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{
				Operation:     "update",
				TreePath:      "README.md",
				ContentReader: strings.NewReader("# Title\n" + commentedLine + "\n"),
			}},
		})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		testPullCreate(t, session, "user2", "test_api_suggestion", false, "master", "suggestion-branch", "API suggestion PR")
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{BaseRepoID: repo.ID, HeadBranch: "suggestion-branch"})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))

		token := getTokenForLoggedInUser(t, session, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteRepository)
		req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, http.MethodPost, fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/test_api_suggestion/pulls/%d/reviews", pr.Issue.Index), &api.CreatePullReviewOptions{
			Event: api.ReviewStateComment,
			Body:  "lint bot",
			Comments: []api.CreatePullReviewComment{
				{Path: "README.md", Body: suggestion, NewLineNum: 2},
				{Path: "README.md", Body: suggestion, OldLineNum: 1}, // old side: stays a plain code block
			},
		}).AddTokenAuth(token)
		review := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), &api.PullReview{})
		assert.Equal(t, api.ReviewStateComment, review.State)
		assert.Equal(t, 2, review.CodeCommentsCount)

		req = NewRequestf(t, http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/repos/user2/test_api_suggestion/pulls/%d/reviews/%d/comments", pr.Issue.Index, review.ID).AddTokenAuth(token)
		comments := DecodeJSON(t, MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK), []*api.PullReviewComment{})
		require.Len(t, comments, 2)
		for _, c := range comments {
			assert.Equal(t, suggestion, c.Body) // stored verbatim, no API-side rewriting
		}

		pages := map[string]string{ // repo/diff/comments.tmpl and view_content/conversation.tmpl
			"files tab":        fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_api_suggestion/pulls/%d/files", pr.Issue.Index),
			"conversation tab": fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_api_suggestion/pulls/%d", pr.Issue.Index),
		}
		for name, link := range pages {
			t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
				doc := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, http.MethodGet, link), http.StatusOK).Body)
				assert.Equal(t, 2, doc.Find(".render-content.markup code.language-suggestion").Length())

				markup := doc.Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]")
				require.Equal(t, 1, markup.Length()) // only the new-side comment
				assert.Equal(t, commentedLine, markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, "Suggested change", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-label", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, replacement+"\n", markup.Find("code.language-suggestion").Text())
			})
		}
	})
}

```text
## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## UML diagrams (D6)
# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the

## What changed

Adds one integration test, `tests/integration/api_pull_review_suggestion_test.go`. A "lint bot" posts a review through the existing `POST /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews` with two code comments that hold a `suggestion` block, one on each side of the diff. The test then checks that:

- the API stores both comment bodies exactly as sent;
- on both the Files tab (`repo/diff/comments.tmpl`) and the Conversation tab (`view_content/conversation.tmpl`), only the new-side comment gets `data-suggestion-original`, set to the commented line, and the "Suggested change" label. That is the hook S1's client code uses to draw the diff;
- the old-side comment stays a plain `code.language-suggestion` block.

No production code changes.

## Why

AC1 of #160: *"Given a review created through the existing API with a suggestion block in a code comment, when viewed in the UI, then it renders as a suggestion … (no API change needed; integration test proves it)."* This is the evidence for the issue's design decision that bots don't need a new create endpoint. The "can be applied" half of AC1 depends on S3 and will be tested with the apply endpoint (AC2).

## Test Evidence

| AC | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC1 (stored as sent) | `TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders`, the review-comments `GET` | Integration | The `suggestion` body the test posts |
| AC1 (renders as suggestion, Files tab) | `TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders/files_tab` | Integration | `"\treturn err"` is line 2 of the README the test writes to the head branch; `"Suggested change"` is the AC wording in #154; the replacement text is the posted block |
| AC1 (renders as suggestion, Conversation tab) | `TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders/conversation_tab` | Integration | Same as above |
| AC1 (old side is not a suggestion) | Both subtests: exactly 1 of the 2 `language-suggestion` blocks is marked | Integration | #154's rule that suggestions apply to the new side only |

This is an integration test rather than a unit test because the AC is about the whole path: API handler → stored comment → page template.

**The test fails without the feature:** with S1's two templates reverted to their `main` versions, both subtests fail (`expected: 1, actual: 0`). With them restored, the test passes.

The client-side diff drawing is S1's code and is covered by its Vitest file (`web_src/js/markup/suggestion.test.ts`).

## CI / manual verification

- `make 'test-integration#TestAPIPullReviewSuggestionRenders'` → `ok gitea.dev/tests/integration 5.1s`
- With S1's templates reverted to `main`: `files_tab` and `conversation_tab` both FAIL, as intended
- `golangci-lint run ./tests/integration/` → `0 issues`; `make fmt` → no changes

## Design

It follows #160's Design Decision ("No new create endpoint: suggestions stay markdown in the comment body"), and this test is the evidence that the decision works.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The PR is stacked on #163, so it can't merge until S1 does. The test checks the server-side hook (`data-suggestion-original`), not the drawn diff, because drawing happens in the browser. A full browser check would need an e2e test, and that is better added once S3's Apply button exists.

**Encountered:** `make lint-go` assumes `golangci-lint` is on `PATH`, and it isn't installed by `make deps-tools`. I ran it with `go run …/golangci-lint@v2.12.2` (the version the Makefile pins). Integration tests also need `make backend` first, or repo creation fails in the pre-receive hook with `gitea: No such file or directory`. Neither was changed here.
